quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive if you can walk in a straight line after drinking.
Your driving is not impaired if you are under the legal blood alcohol limit.
Alcohol harms your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol harms your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol hurts your judgment. You need good judgment to respond to things you see on the road. Even small amounts of alcohol can make it harder to drive safely, even if you are under the legal limit.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to all vehicles coming from the opposite direction. This includes bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: Before you change lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your traffic lane.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check behind you. Look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicle is in the lane you want to enter. Also check that no other driver is moving into the same spot from a different lane.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed on the side next to the solid yellow line.
Allowed on the side next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed on the side next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When the center has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line, passing is allowed from the broken line side and not allowed from the solid line side.

questions.question: As vehicle speed increases, stopping distances and crash severity:
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: While driving, look 10 to 15 seconds ahead of you:

options.text: And focus on the middle of the road.
Because it is required by law.

questions.explanation: Scan ahead 10 to 15 seconds so you can see hazards early and avoid last-minute moves. Staring at the road right in front of your vehicle is dangerous.

questions.question: On a slippery road, keep a following distance that is:
questions.explanation: It takes longer to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Keep extra distance between you and the car ahead when driving on slippery roads.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Drive faster to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam lights. If fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: Which of these factors affects how fast someone absorbs alcohol?
questions.explanation: Weight, biological sex, the amount of food in your stomach, and how many alcoholic drinks you have had all affect alcohol absorption. Only time can remove alcohol from your system.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign means:
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards or special conditions ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: Night driving is more dangerous than daytime driving because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: Poor visibility and glare from oncoming headlights mean you cannot see as far ahead at night as during the day. Always use headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: When the road first gets wet from rain, it is slippery. On a slippery road, you should:

options.text: Test your tire traction while going uphill.
Look less far ahead of your vehicle.

questions.explanation: Wet roads do not give your tires good grip, so drive slowly. To prevent skidding, avoid fast turns or sudden stops.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways:
questions.explanation: While large vehicles have special wind problems, strong wind can affect all drivers. Wind can lower visibility by blowing dust and dirt, and it can also physically push a vehicle.

questions.question: If dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should drive slowly and turn on your:
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights anytime you cannot see other vehicles. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles stop faster than other vehicles, and you need room to stop if the rider brakes or falls. Motorcycles are hard to see at night because they only have one tail light.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross illegally in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Do not have to stop for them.

questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians at all times, even if they are crossing where they should not be.

questions.question: This sign is a:
questions.explanation: A triangle pointing downward is always a yield sign. Be ready to slow down or stop when you see a yield sign.

questions.question: You can legally drive with an open alcoholic beverage container only if it is:
questions.explanation: Keep any open alcoholic beverage in the trunk or where passengers do not sit. An open drink in the glove compartment is not allowed. These rules do not apply to non-driving passengers in buses, taxis, campers, or motor homes.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should check:

options.text: Over your left or right shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: At an intersection with stop signs on all four corners, you must give the right-of-way to a driver who:
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles should go through in the order they arrived. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: This sign tells you the road ahead:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves right and then curves left.

questions.question: What is an important step when turning?

options.text: Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: Before turning, look behind and to both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Slow down to safely complete the turn.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign tells drivers what they must do. Where this sign is posted, turning right is not allowed.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, you should:

options.text: Do not drive through. Turn around and take another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through. Turn around and take another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive on a flooded road. The water may hide hazards you cannot see. If you see flooding, turn around and find another route.

questions.question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:

options.text: Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
Other drivers when they slow down.

questions.explanation: Trucks need more space to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Press hard on the gas pedal.

questions.explanation: When backing up, place your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly through the rear window. Mirrors do not show what is directly behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Locks the front wheels, causing loss of steering control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels, causing loss of steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock your front wheels and cause you to lose steering control. Drive at a safe speed to avoid hard braking.

questions.question: California's Move Over law requires:

options.text: All vehicles to stay in the right lane at all times.
Trucks to use the left lane.
All vehicles to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle is stopped on the side of the road with its lights on, you must move out of the lane next to it if you can do so safely. If you cannot move over, slow down and drive carefully. This rule also applies to tow trucks and Department of Transportation vehicles.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Pull to the right and go around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until they have crossed before you proceed.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means:

options.text: Stop and wait for the green light.

questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. After you stop, you may proceed if it is safe, following all right-of-way rules.

questions.question: The speed limit at an uncontrolled railroad crossing is:
questions.explanation: When you are within 100 feet of an uncontrolled railroad crossing and cannot see the tracks 400 feet ahead in both directions, the speed limit is 15 mph.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that you are leaving a divided highway and entering a road with traffic going both ways.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, match the speed of the traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with no warning devices and cannot see 400 feet down the tracks. The speed limit is:
questions.explanation: When you are within 100 feet of a railroad crossing and cannot see 400 feet down the tracks in both directions, the speed limit is 15 mph. You can drive faster if the crossing has gates, warning signals, or a flagger.

questions.question: You are on a freeway with a 65 mph speed limit. Heavy traffic is moving at 35 mph. The best speed for your vehicle is most likely:
questions.explanation: Crashes happen more often when drivers travel at different speeds. Drive at the same speed as other traffic on the road, unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: Temporary signs in construction and work areas have:

options.text: A red background with green writing.
An orange background with black writing.
A yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: An orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have an orange background with black writing or symbols.
